items.title: Coral reefs cover under 1% of the ocean but host around 25% of marine species
items.claim: What proportion of marine biodiversity do coral reefs support?

options.text: Around 25% of all marine species live on coral reefs, which cover less than 1% of the ocean floor — perhaps the most concentrated biodiversity hotspot on Earth
Coral reefs support only the species visible to divers

items.reveal:
Reefs occupy around 284,000 km² globally — under 0.1% of the ocean. The Great Barrier Reef is 2,300 km long. Species counts: around 4,000 fish species, 800 reef-building coral species, plus uncounted invertebrates.

Mass bleaching events (1998, 2010, 2014-17, 2024) have hit major reef systems. The Great Barrier Reef has experienced bleaching in 2016, 2017, 2020, 2022 and 2024. Some 50% of shallow corals on the GBR died in the 2016 event.

Reefs also provide coastal protection, fisheries and tourism value estimated at hundreds of billions of dollars annually.
items.why: Conservation priorities follow concentration. A small fraction of the planet holds an outsized share of biodiversity — losing reefs means losing whole ecosystems, not just iconic species.

items.title: The Indian monsoon is driven by land-sea temperature contrast
items.claim: What causes the South Asian summer monsoon?

options.text: Differential heating: in summer, the Asian continent heats up faster than the Indian Ocean, creating a low-pressure zone that draws in moist oceanic air, reversed in winter
The Earth's gravitational interaction with the Moon

items.reveal:
From June to September, the Tibetan Plateau heats intensely; low-level winds reverse and blow from southwest, bringing moisture from the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal. The Indian subcontinent receives perhaps 80% of its annual rainfall in these months.

The Himalayas force orographic lifting, producing the wettest places on Earth (Mawsynram, Cherrapunji — Meghalaya). The Western Ghats also lift the air.

Climate change is shifting monsoon onset and intensity. The Indian Meteorological Department's date of onset has varied by weeks in recent decades. Around 1.5 billion people depend on the monsoon for agriculture.
items.why: Monsoon variability is one of the highest-stakes climate signals on Earth. A failed monsoon means famine; a strong one means floods. The mechanism (differential heating) is testable physics — but its variability is poorly forecast.
